sources.entry: Build A Face Detector using OpenCV and Deep Learning

summary.title: Face detection with OpenCV and deep learning
summary.one_liner: You learn how to use OpenCV's bundled pre-trained Caffe deep learning face detector (SSD with ResNet base) for face detection in images and webcam/video streams, as a more accurate replacement for Haar cascades.
keywords: detect faces in images opencv python
takeaways: OpenCV's dnn module ships a pre-trained Caffe face detector (SSD with ResNet base), not found in the samples folder without the weight files.
Load the detector with cv2.dnn.readNetFromCaffe using the prototxt and caffemodel files, then build a 300x300 blob with blobFromImage.
Filter detections by a confidence threshold (default 0.5) and draw bounding boxes with confidence labels.
The same code can be adapted to video or webcam by reading frames from VideoStream and drawing on each frame.
The page notes alternatives: Haar cascades (fast, more false positives), dlib HOG and CNN, and MTCNN.
summary.summary: The article reveals that OpenCV (since 3.3) includes a deep learning face detector built on the SSD framework with a ResNet base network, and explains where its Caffe prototxt and weight files are found. It walks through a Python script to detect faces in a single image using cv2.dnn.readNetFromCaffe and blobFromImage, looping over detections and drawing boxes above a confidence threshold. A second script applies the same approach to a webcam or video stream using imutils' VideoStream. The post closes with a short comparison of other face detection methods (Haar cascades, dlib HOG/CNN, MTCNN) and promotes a paid course, which is not technical content.
